content.value_statement: Data-heavy React apps need consistent dark interfaces that remain readable and maintainable. This skill provides Tailwind, TypeScript, and motion patterns for polished dashboards.
actual_capabilities: Lists React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript, and Framer Motion setup steps.
Provides Tailwind theme tokens for dark colors, spacing, shadows, and animation.
Shows HTML metadata, PWA manifest, and favicon structure examples.
Defines CSS utilities for glass cards, panels, overlays, inputs, focus states, and scrollbars.
Includes TypeScript React examples for routing, page transitions, and motion variants.
limitations: It is documentation, not an installable component package.
It does not include actual asset files, icons, or font binaries.
It uses example app names and URLs that must be replaced.
It does not validate accessibility, browser support, or production performance.

use_cases.title: Start a Dashboard
use_cases.description: Create a dark Vite React dashboard with consistent Tailwind tokens and motion patterns.

use_cases.title: Translate a Design System
use_cases.description: Convert a dark visual system into implementable colors, spacing, typography, and surface patterns.

use_cases.title: Standardize Internal Tools
use_cases.description: Build admin panels with shared layout, component, and interaction conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter App
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-ui-dark-ts to plan a new Vite React dashboard. Include setup steps, folder structure, and required packages.

prompt_templates.title: Style a Dashboard Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-ui-dark-ts to design a dark analytics dashboard with cards, tabs, forms, and motion states.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt Existing Components
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration of current React code
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply frontend-ui-dark-ts patterns to my current React components. Keep behavior unchanged and update Tailwind classes consistently.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Production UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my TypeScript React admin UI against frontend-ui-dark-ts. Identify token drift, accessibility gaps, and animation issues.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a dark dashboard foundation.
output_examples.output: A setup checklist with Vite, React, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, routing, folders, and dark theme tokens.

output_examples.input: A user asks to improve an admin panel surface style.
output_examples.output: A design pass covering glass panels, borders, contrast, spacing, focus states, and card hierarchy.

output_examples.input: A user asks for animation guidance.
output_examples.output: A motion plan for page transitions, hover feedback, staggered lists, and reduced motion considerations.

best_practices: Replace placeholder app names, URLs, and images before release.
Test contrast, keyboard focus, and reduced motion with real users.
Keep design tokens centralized before adding page-specific styles.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder metadata into production.
Do not treat glass effects as a substitute for readable contrast.
Do not add animations that block navigation, forms, or data scanning.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete app?
faq.answer: No. It gives patterns and examples for building a dark React interface.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it target?
faq.answer: It targets React with TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, React Router, and Framer Motion.

faq.question: Can I use it with existing components?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it to align Tailwind classes, tokens, surfaces, and motion patterns.

faq.question: Does it include accessibility checks?
faq.answer: It includes focus and touch target guidance, but you must run full accessibility validation.

faq.question: Are the example URLs production ready?
faq.answer: No. Replace example.com URLs, app names, and social images before publishing.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands and examples, but the user decides what to run.
